title: Profile Scoreboard Hardening
lede: The Scoreboard now keeps privacy checks, season ownership, pagination, rankings, and touch targets consistent across the API, web profile, and native profile.

stats.n: Measured in the matched desktop captures; all controls also measured 40px at 390×844
Route, service, digest, web source, and native wiring tests

sections.heading: Matched visual change
sections.note: Same local Preview account, user, season data, theme, viewport, and crop. Only the Scoreboard implementation differs.

pairs.title: Filters and breakdown control
pairs.beforeCap: Result filters measured 28px, the sport filter 32px, and the breakdown control 30.7px.
pairs.afterCap: All four interaction types now share a 40px minimum target without changing the surrounding data hierarchy.

changes.h: Pagination could revive a finished cursor
changes.was: A null final-page cursor fell back to the original response cursor, while overlapping or stale requests could append repeated rows.
changes.now: Cursor ownership distinguishes not-yet-loaded from end-of-list, aborts stale requests, blocks overlap, deduplicates pages, and exposes retry without discarding rendered rows.

changes.was: Web and iOS sent a hard-coded 2026–27 season, creating a rollover drift point.
changes.now: Both clients omit season unless one is explicitly requested, leaving the authenticated API as the default-season owner.

changes.was: A collaborator denial path could query a requested target before rejecting access.
changes.now: The route rejects unauthorized cross-user requests before target lookup, while keeping self, staff, admin, visibility, and not-found behavior covered by the role matrix.

changes.was: Best venue favored raw win rate, so a 1–0 venue could outrank a sustained 6–1 record; area ordering depended on encounter order.
changes.now: Web and iOS rank venue strength by win margin, then rate and volume; worked areas follow the canonical product order.

verification: Web gates: TypeScript, full ESLint, docs/codemap verification, migration-prefix validation, and npm run build:app passed.
Native gates: 10 focused XCTest cases, iOS project parity, drift audit, audit-gap inventory, and a full iPhone 16 Pro simulator build passed.
Authenticated web: All/Losses state verified for Nolan; default request omitted season; desktop and 390×844 layouts had zero console errors.
Authenticated native: All/Wins state verified for Maddy on iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5.
notes: The live Nolan fixture has only one resolved result page, so the load-more failure state was verified through regression/source tests rather than forced against live data.
No production deployment, schema migration, or API response-shape change is part of this slice.
